text_fidelity_a:
Retrospec Stash Rack Bike Floor Stand Bicycle Storage Organizer This is a simple and easy to assembly bike rack. It works perfect for us.

it took me all of 15 minutes to put together for 3 bikes. I love that you have the option to expand it to 5 bikes if needed. (more on that later). The instructions were easy to follow (I've included a pic).

What's in the box: This comes with everything you need to assemble your frame, even a little hex wrench which is the only tool you need other than your two hands. All the pieces are nicely packed in the box and have plastic over them to protect them from getting scuffed up in the box. Your box should have 2 frame tube ends, 10 frame tubes, 10 wheel arms, 5 wheel arm binders, 20 hex-head screws, and one hex wrench.

Assembly: The bottom bars for the frame pretty much snap together with little push in metal buttons to hold them in place (see pic). The holes for the buttons are nice and oblong so you have room to twist/maneuver them when attaching the wheel arms to get the holes aligned when screwing them in. The only slight issue I had is the hex screw heads. A few of them seemed to easily strip when I was doing the last few turns with the provided hex wrench. I was not even tightening them very tight so there was not a lot of torque. I figured they were probably just cheap screws, but they still did the job fine. The screws you can twist by hand easily once you get the holes aligned correctly then just use the hex wrench to finish up. Once you have the wheel arms attached the wheel arm binders easily attach at the top of the wheel arms but squeezing them together slightly then just slide the binder down next to the frame once it is on. And that's all there is to it!

using the stand: we have 3 bikes - 2 mountain bikes and 1 road bike. I thought I may have to add a spacer to the frame since the mountain bike handle bars will not fit if the two of them are right next to each other in this stand. I did try putting one in backward, with the rear wheel in the stand, but the bike stand arms were too narrow for wheel and derailer to completely fit into the stand. however, my road bike is small enough that it fits just under the mountain bike handle bars. putting that in the middle solved the issue! Now we have all three bikes neatly parked in a corner of the garage rather than leaning against the wall and boxes. yay! And if we happen to acquire more bikes, we can always expand it.

Overall this is a decent, simple bike stand that does what we need.
text_fidelity_b: Retrospec Stash Rack Bike Floor Stand Bicycle Storage Organizer

text_fidelity_a:
GoSports Fitness Core Hub Plank Board with Smart Phone Integration for Full Body Workouts - Blue or Red So far so good with this GoSports Core Hub Fitness Plank Board with Smart Phone Integration. I’d seen a similar product in commercials and wondered if it would actually work for planking - or was it a gimmick. When I had the chance to grab this GoSports Core Hub Fitness Plank Board with Smart Phone Integration I took it, hoping it would add to my workout options. For various reasons I prefer not to plank directly on the ground, so would this be of help? The answer for me is, yes. As I continue to adjust to using it.

It arrives with the platform itself, pump, and instructions. One assembles the platform simply by pumping air into the ball on the bottom. My wife and I found this was a two person job - the long needle easily went in, however, it also easily pumped out until I had her hold it in place. At that point the ball quickly and easily pumped to full size. Pulling the needle out the air stayed in and there was no leaking - with nothing to plug it - and a week later holds the air perfectly. They included a second pin for the end of the pump - great if the first breaks or is lost, but we’ve found the first one wouldn’t even come off after we secured it.

There is a plastic covering on the phone “t” so don’t forget to remove it. It easily comes off and the foam under holds the phone in place just fine - though I haven’t used the phone or any app for working out at this point - I do have it there for stop watch.

I’ve put some pounds on since surgery so I wondered how it would hold the weight and so far it’s fine. I don’t feel any weakness or bowing or any issue in holding me up. As a shorter guy with shorter arm length I do find that positioning my arms in a spot to make placement comfortable is not exact. In fact, I end up testing my forearms a bit to hold on. And it’s taking time to find the best spot for being comfortable on the platform. Plus having the platform lay right in oder to balance correctly. Still working it, but also, still getting a solid workout. In fact I come away each time feeling the burn and it’s been a solid way to plank. It can be used in either the kneeling or full out, extended leg position and while I’ve only done it fully extended, I can see the benefits to both options.

So, does the movement and/or height add to the benefit of planking? I have to think it does. I like being up off the floor and having a nice, comfortable surface under my arms. As for the movement, it does work the fuller core area and I feel the burn in more than just one spot. I’ve only done this for a week, twice a day most days, and I’m doing better at time at the end of that week. I will maybe add in the app-games, but right now that is not my personal interest - but I can see how it could add to the fun (I’m not a gamer).

Any cons? So far it’s a little too early to know overall - will the board last, how does the app work...
I did notice there is a ’sound’ when laying on the board under the forearms. It seems like it might indicate the surface material could separate from the hard plastic base.

I do have an issue in reaching the handles under the platform - for grip I hold the side of the platform. It might be nice to have a grip along the side one can hold onto other than these two handles.

As long as the ball holds up - and I so far do not see why it won’t hold up - it can be a good, solid exercise platform. But that foam on the top needs to also remain. If that comes off, it will affect the platform itself. So far it’s fine, but again, what does that sound mean - other times I’ve heard it things have separated.

In the end I so far believe this GoSports Core Hub Fitness Plank Board with Smart Phone Integration is a great find and will help me with my workouts and to improve physically. I’m enjoying the experience and I’m enjoying the possibilities of how to continue planking in a fun manner. So yes, I do like this GoSports Core Hub Fitness Plank Board with Smart Phone Integration and happy to give it a 5 star rating.
text_fidelity_b: GoSports Fitness Core Hub Plank Board with Smart Phone Integration for Full Body Workouts - Blue or Red

text_fidelity_a:
SPYPOINT CELL-LINK Universal CELL LINK Trail Camera Adapter Turns Any Trail Camera to Cellular Camera | Images Sent to Your App by Connecting Through Trail Cam SD Card Slot(Motion SENSOR) While this could be a serious upgrade for an Old, photo-only trail cam that doesn't take videos, there are several drawbacks to using this device, and slightly misleading info that makes it seem, or you would think, it does more than it can. Not true, it's actually a very limited, though clever, device.

First of all, as to its 'near universal' fit, it ONLY works in cameras with a full-size HC-SD card slot. That means it will not fit if your camera has a micro SD card slot. They say this, true enough, but hunters/ cameras seem to use the term SD indiscriminately. They say there are no plans to develop a micro SD adapter (that connects the cell link to your camera. )

Second, if your camera takes videos, you will never see any of them, they are not saved anywhere, and as they say, they aren't transmitted and you won't see them in the app, either. Videos are out, gone, might as well turn that setting off in your camera. It will not copy, store or transmit videos, and with your camera's memory slot taken up by the adapter, there is No Video Capability of the camera with this attached.

Third (geeks, this is for you), there is no two-way connectivity between your camera and the (yes, wait for it! ) Micro SD card you must install in the cell link. In other words, the cell link extracts still images from your camera, and stores them in the micro SD card you supply on the cell link (for the cell link to later transmit), but your camera can never see those images again, it's just a one way dump. So if your camera has any high falutin functions (good screen, wifi, etc.) you'd like to use in the field, it will never be able to read the images it captured. Gone (to cell link. )

I did not try to reproduce the cable-crimp problem, I tested this all with open compartments.

The manual is Excellent. The app and storage plans seem very good. It was easy to set up, and even in my remote neck of the woods I was able to get connected to Verizon in a few seconds (my phone cannot often boast the same.) I used a third party antenna booster (at 1/4 the cost of spypoints, it worked excellently boosting 1-2 bars. ) It does have an external 12V jack for a battery or appropriate solar panel/ battery.

The concept is excellent. The manufacturing seems first class. And it's pretty cheap! If you've got old hunting cameras you don't want to be going to check, just know where the game is, this could be very valuable. If you're thinking you can kluge some high tech security system out of this, you will probably also be disappointed. Like I was, and returned it.
text_fidelity_b: SPYPOINT CELL-LINK Universal CELL LINK Trail Camera Adapter Turns Any Trail Camera to Cellular Camera | Images Sent to Your App by Connecting Through Trail Cam SD Card Slot(Motion SENSOR)

text_fidelity_a:
Tenaya Lake Lighted Fast Pitch Cabin Tent You can stand up in it. All of it. The ceiling is super high. Laugh at all the other dome tents that require crawling into, that you might be able to awkwardly stand just in the middle!

The door is wonderful. Going in and out of the tent has never been easier. It actually acts stiff like a hinged door would, making quick pops in and out so much easier than with a floppy zipper door. This of course does have a zipper the whole way around (which works smoother than my other cheaper tents) with flaps to block rain. Not only is the door action flawless, I was impressed with how it kept bugs out without using the zipper. While we definitely zipped up when not using it for extended periods, we could easily rely on the velcro and stiffness popped up under the rain flaps to make a fairly decent seal. It wouldn't keep tiny crawly bugs out, but it definitely does a good job keeping flying bugs out.

The windows in this thing are awesome. There's like seven of them and they simply zip up and down as panels. They're great to gaze out of on a lazy afternoon. They work well to keep rain out, too.

The rainfly (roof) also works well. Although it seems like it doesn't cover much but the top, it doesn't really need to do much more. In fact, we didn't even use the rope tie-downs for it - the velcro seemed to keep it plenty taut. We had moderate short bouts of rain overnight and it was 100% dry inside.

The closets do add a nice bit of space, though they look a bit weird on the 6-person version. They're nice to shove things out of the way. There's so much space in this tent compared to other tents I've been in. My last "4-person" tent isn't really that comfortable for two people. This is luxurious for two people. We called it our little airbnb in the woods.

Also, I LOVE THE COLORS. The thing just looks awesome.

Setup is moderately more complicated than a simple 2-rod dome tent but it's actually quite clever and intuitive. I set it up by myself (awkwardly in my basement, it was wet out) as practice. Basically, a spidery bit arcs out 6 (I know, not 8, not a real spider) flexible rods, which meet in a macaroni-type elbow at each corner and mid-front and back. Stiff poles prop up each side/corner and meet at the elbow. That's really the fundamentals. The rest is just clips and rainfly and extra rods for the door and closets. It's REALLY fast with two people, especially if you know what to do.

The paper instructions are kinda hard to parse, so I definitely recommend a practice setup so you're not caught in a rainstorm doing it for the first time. Youtube videos were helpful for me here.

One of my flexible rods actually shattered as soon as I tried to use it. Luckily it was just for one of the closets - not a big deal at all, it just looked weird on the outside. I'll have to figure out how to get a replacement. I hope that isn't happening for one of the structural rods on anybody's.

I didn't originally realize there was a 6-person version of this tent and almost bought the 8-person. There's only two of us and I'm really glad I went with the 6. Not only is it much cheaper, it's still got loads of space even with a queen airbed in there. I'm sure if we needed to accommodate another person or two it would have been little issue and still have been comfy. (Yes, I'm sure you could cram 6 people in if you really wanted.)

I'm really enamored with this tent. It was my girlfriend's first time camping and we had an amazing 3 days and nights with this tent!
text_fidelity_b: Tenaya Lake Lighted Fast Pitch Cabin Tent

text_fidelity_a:
Stormy Kromer Rancher Cap - Winter Thinsulate Wool Hat with Fleece Earflap This is my fourth "serious" cold weather hat purchase in recent years. I bought this from another vendor because at the time Amazon did not have my needed size 7-3/4 in Black. I normally wear 7-5/8, but ordered a bit larger as recommended by others. I will compare it to three other hats:

1.) Mountain Hardwear Dome Perignon, XL - Windblock fleece that fits over my large noggin and protects my ears and much of my neck. In this comparison, this is my first, warmest and still most favorite hat if I don't need sun protection. Wish it didn't have the large logo on front! Quiet under a hoody. Can store easily in many pockets.
2.) Outdoor Research Rando, XL - Goretex shell & inner fleece hat with earflaps that fold under cap. Smallish, wire frame bill can be bent up, offers some eye protection, but not enough when sun is low in sky. Wish it didn't have the large "OR" logo on front. Noisy under a hoody. Most portable, take anywhere hat, but ultimately not as good as...
3.) REI Crestrails Winter Cap, XL (2015 model & doesn't seem to be available this year) - My favorite overall hat. Almost as warm as Mountain Hardwear Dome Perignon, but with long bill for sun protection, and REI's proprietary wind/rain shell over cozy fleece layer. Also, drawstring can adjust earflap snugness and keep hat from blowing off head in strong winds. Has very small logo, so doesn't stand out. Noisy under a hoody. Stores well in down or storm shell pockets.

And, now we come to the mighty Stormy Kromer Rancher, which I had high hopes for. I expected with all that wool and bulk that it would be warmer than the others. Making exact comparisons about relative warmth is challenging because the weather can vary and how physically active I am makes such judgement tricky. Still, I got the consistent experience that this hat isn't as warm as any of the other three, especially if there is any wind at all!

It is by far the bulkiest, largest hat of the bunch, and as many have commented, may not be all that flattering to one's head at least in urban environments -- not that I care if the hat is functional. There is a fairly stiff band around the inside perimeter that tended to press uncomfortably on the side frames of my wrap-around sunglasses (Serengeti Maestrale & Erice - love 'em both!). Didn't care for that, and none of the other hats had this problem.

The earflaps didn't hug my ears very well, and the wind blows right through them. Very disappointed in that, and adjusting the front bow-tie didn't make much difference, except when really tight, but then it was too tight for my head. I eventually discovered that if I left the flaps folded up, then pulled the band over my ears, it still covered almost all my ear, but with two layers. This arrangement is warmer and snugger, but still lets some wind through. Perhaps I can put a dark band of plastic between the layers for wind protection? Hmmm, I'll try that.

OK, so what do I like? The construction and materials are top notch, and it seems a good value for an American made product. I like the lack of a logo -- though the big size draws attention in other ways. The material is very quiet under a down hoody or storm shell hood. No swishing sounds here.

Overall, I have all I need in the REI Crestrails and Mountain Hardwear Dome Perignon. The OR is the most minimal of all hats, and one that I can keep as a spare in the car, backpack or camera bag. The Stormy Kromer, unfortunately, was a $50 purchase I wish I had not made based on my experience with other hats.

Of course, it may work for you, as witnessed by the many 5-star reviews here and elsewhere.
text_fidelity_b: Stormy Kromer Rancher Cap - Winter Thinsulate Wool Hat with Fleece Earflap

text_fidelity_a:
Travoy, Compact Folding Cargo Bike Trailer Download the manual from the Burley website.

This is our second Travoy trailer. The other is still in use after 10 years. The new Travoy has some substantial upgrades:

• The new “kickstand” design keeps the trailer upright when parked with a load. The old one would tip over.
• New seatpost hitch allows a single hitch to be shared among two or more bikes. With the old one you had to buy more hitches.
• The tow arm now extends to accommodate rear bike racks and larger MTB wheels.
• Tow arm is now padded with foam for hand comfort.

The entire time we owned our first Travoy we mistakenly believed we should have chosen a flatbed instead. We recently bought a flatbed and don’t use it; bought a second Travoy as a backup. If all you do is local errands the Travoy is by far the easiest and best. If you tour or travel dirt roads a flatbed might be a better choice but you should want both a flatbed plus the Travoy because the Travoy is easier for local errands which are far more common.

The bags that are dedicated for use with the Travoy are costly and do not hold enough. Instead, wheel your Travoy into Target or Walmart and choose the largest clothes hamper that fits the Travoy form factor (see photo). Attach that hamper with three ratcheting tie-downs or four high quality, ADJUSTABLE bungees. Do not skimp on quality or number.

PROS:
• Lightweight, 10lbs +/-
• No tools or setup required. Screw the hitch onto your seatpost with the T-bold and you’re done.
• Folds to easily fit in a backseat, a trunk or an airline overhead.
• Holds up to $125 in groceries with the large hamper attached. Mind the maximum weight restriction (60lbs) and pack the heaviest items at the bottom (66% of load) and lighter items at the top (33%).
• With the Travoy you don’t have to bend over quite as far to reach cargo.
• Comes with a storage/carrying bag (although it’s mostly useless for carrying cargo).

CONS:
• You must adjust your riding style slightly. The Travoy is stable on level pavement but may tip over at significant road imperfections or surface debris. Slow down and approach handicapped ramps and driveways exactly at 90 degrees (perpendicular) to avoid catching a wheel on their raised shoulders. Avoid potholes and debris entirely. You’ll grow accustomed to this over time and it will not bother you. If the Travoy DOES tip, it doesn’t take the bike with it.
• If you run with the stock tires and tubes be prepared for flats. The availability of high quality 12.5” inch tires and tubes is extremely limited. All the tires from Asia that we tried are no good, even dangerous. We found very high quality 12.5 inch tires from the German manufacturer “Schwalbe” (available here on Amazon). Schwalbe currently offers the “Road Cruiser” for street and the “Black Jack” for trails and off-road (12/2020).
• 12.5” thorn resistant tubes are available here on Amazon but the Travoy 12.5 inch wheels require a 45 degree valve; otherwise there is not enough room to attach a pump or even a pump hose. These thorn resistant tubes had straight valves. To accommodate this shortcoming we found a "Air Inflator Hose Adapter" here on Amazon. Although it just barely fits, we can use it with both our floor pump and our road pump.

TIPS:
• In addition to thorn resistant tubes, we use the “Mr. Tuffy”-brand tire inserts on all our bike and trailer wheels (here on Amazon). Flats are now a very rare occurrence and we ride among numerous desert thorns.
• When using the hamper it is easy to cut a neon yellow reflective vest into three sections (left front, right front and back) and attach the sections to the hamper (left side, right side and rear, see photo).
• Reflective flags and flagpoles with mounts that fit your hamper are available here on Amazon. The flagpole we bought is high enough so that the flag can be seen above the level of a parked car (see photo). For added safety we now use this flag and pole on our bikes even without the trailer.
• When the hamper is inappropriate we use a cargo net. The cargo net is also handy if your hamper is overflowing.

Leave a comment if you have questions.
text_fidelity_b: Travoy, Compact Folding Cargo Bike Trailer

text_fidelity_a:
Intex Challenger Kayak, Inflatable Kayak Set with Aluminum Oars and High Output Air-Pump This thing is amazing!! I've taken it out 6 times over the last month, for 2–5 mile jaunts, at local city lakes and sheltered bays, and a couple lakes in a National Park. At this point it's already worth its price: if it failed next outing (I don't think it will) I'd still be happy with it. For less than 100 bucks I have the ability to visit little islands inside lakes, get unbelievable views from the water, and explore wetlands and sloughs that landlubbers can't get to. I can't get over the novelty of launching, docking at some isolated rock beach or island to eat a snack, then coming back over the water. And having the ability to do this where there are no concessionaires almost feels like cheating! The experience is just that amazing. Not to mention ease of transport and storage.

As far as seaworthiness: yes, it tracks poorly even with the skeg but that just means more rotational practice for you. Stable in lake waves and jetski wakes, I've never felt close to capsizing. It's slow. Will blow with the wind if you let it, but you can easily paddle against it. It works, and it'll get you there.

Setup and teardown is easy but it does take some time. The pump is fine and it will inflate faster than you think. For durability: all components feels very heavy and solid, it's like bounce house material. The valves feel strong and actually take some effort to release the air. I take care not to beach the kayak, or set up/tear down on any surface too rocky or spiky. I also take lengths to dry it afterwards: I point fans at it for a few hours, making sure to get the inside crevices dry. I feel optimistic it'll be fine for a while.

Standard hacks: Get a large IKEA blue bag to carry the actual deflated kayak, use the included (flimsy) bag for the other components, pump, your PFD. Don't inflate the seat-bottom for more vertical leg room.

When researching this, I talked to 2 paddling-adventure friends and inflatable kayaks are perfectly respectable and even the choice of some extreme adventurers: see Audrey Sutherland's amazing books and adventures, and look up Grabner inflatables. Enjoy!!!
text_fidelity_b: Intex Challenger Kayak, Inflatable Kayak Set with Aluminum Oars and High Output Air-Pump

text_fidelity_a: INVOKER Ultralight Inflatable Camping Sleeping Pad - Mat with Built-in Foot Pump, Lightweight Compact Air Mattress, Best Sleeping Pads for Backpacking Travel Hiking Beach, Fully Inflate in 25s I'm not a hiker, but I do have an SUV tent, an air mattress that fits the back of the SUV and now an air pillow.  I'm a bit different than most folks because I actually sleep on a 20" tall queen size air mattress every night and have done so for the past two years.  The thing is, with the air mattress I can move and sleep in may different positions and my body feels supported.  That's not exactly how or why I use a pillow.  Again, I'm not like most people - I have been sleeping with a 100% down pillow for so many years I can't even remember when I bought my first one.  I mention this because of the way I use a pillow when sleeping - it is molded, puffed out and reformed several times during the night.  That just can't happen with this air pillow.  For me, it serves more as a back prop for sitting up and reading on the bed.  Nice and firm, it gives me back support while sitting up in bed.  It does store well in the very small case it comes in and that's perfect!  As I have gotten older and had to move when I didn't really want to but circumstances made me, I have become addicted to "nomadic furniture" that is easier to move than traditional furniture.  An air pillow does fit within my parameters of small and packable!  Same with my bed - not quite a small, but certainly nothing like lugging around a heavy, floppy queen size mattress and box springs!  So, all in all, I am pleased with this air pillow at least for what I will use it for.

text_fidelity_a: BUCKLOS LUTU 26/27.5/29 Air MTB Suspension Fork, Rebound Adjust Straight Tube 28.6mm QR 9mm Travel 120mm Manual/Crown Lockout Mountain Bike Forks, Ultralight Gas Shock XC Bicycle As a replacement for the worn out OEM coil fork on my 29’er, this has been great.  The improvement in ride quality is very evident.  An area I frequently ride has sections where tracked vehicles have left long stretches of washboard terrain, which previously were a jarring, miserable riding experience.  Now, they’re really barely noticeable.  I have only a couple gripes.  The fork comes with absolutely nothing in the way of instructions for installation, maintenance or setup, or even contact info.  However, installing it is extremely simple, except for the brake cable issue mentioned below.  And there’s quite a bit of torsional flex in the fork. I would hesitate to tackle any black diamonds with this fork, but for intermediate trail riding, it’s a nice, affordable upgrade.  As mentioned by several other reviewers, you may have issues with the brake caliper needing a lot of patient adjustment to prevent the rotor banging into the caliper body; this is a pretty basic manufacturing issue, and a millimeter or so extra distance between the brake posts and the axle drop out would be helpful.  Be aware that the fork is likely to be quite a bit longer than OEM forks on most low- to mid-range bikes (it was almost 3.5” longer than the original on mine) and this does manifest itself in a changed geometry and frame height, as well as necessitating a longer front brake cable.
text_fidelity_b: BUCKLOS LUTU 26/27.5/29 Air MTB Suspension Fork, Rebound Adjust Straight Tube 28.6mm QR 9mm Travel 120mm Manual/Crown Lockout Mountain Bike Forks, Ultralight Gas Shock XC Bicycle

AKUSAKO Camping Propane Heater - 2 In 1 Outdoor Portable Gas Heater & Stove Included Tent Heaters + Propane Hose Kit for Regulator Applicable For Ice Fishing Backpacking Hiking Hunting(Orange) Actually, I think this is a good buy. It has a piezo ignition that works. It puts out plenty of heat. Although I don't envision cooking on it I can see where it would handle the task ok but I would be worried about boilovers putting out the flame. This thing puts out a ton of heat and is sufficiently adjustable in output.

Pros. It easily lights. Puts out sufficient heat and does so at 360 degrees all around. It is larger than expected which I think is a good thing. The base seems stable. The output is adjustable.

Cons. The biggest fault I find is the warning on the outside of the heater which states "For Outdoor Use Only" when in fact the Title or Heading states, "AKUSAKO Camping Propane Heater - 2 In 1 Outdoor Portable Gas Heater & Stove Included Tent Heaters " Note it says "tent heater." So, now I am not so sure. It would likely be fine but I would not operate it indoors without a CO and Oxygen monitor, which I own anyway. It is not a good idea to operate any propane device in a tent without the monitors anyway.

The rubber feet (3) are all stripped out. The rubber feet screw through a fairly thin metal plate that was stripped out at the factory. Note that this can probably be easily remedied by using a slightly larger sheet metal screw instead of what appears to be a small wood screw, just don't overtighten.
text_fidelity_b: AKUSAKO Camping Propane Heater - 2 In 1 Outdoor Portable Gas Heater & Stove Included Tent Heaters + Propane Hose Kit for Regulator Applicable For Ice Fishing Backpacking Hiking Hunting(Orange)

TETON Sports Outfitter XXL Camping Cot; Camping Cots for Adults; Folding Cot Bed; Easy Set Up; Storage Bag Included I'd prefer to give this cot 2 1/2 stars, but there are no 1/2 stars available in the rating process. so, I gave it 2.

The positives: I didn't find it that difficult to set up. The trick is to follow the instructions (do one corner, then the opposite corner on the other side of the cot, then repeat the process). And it's very important to make sure each side of the hinge brackets properly encase the legs as the cot is being expanded. (You'll understand what I mean if you buy this cot.) Lastly, it's wide and should give most people sufficient room to move a little when sleeping on it.

The negatives: I actually didn't find the canvas to be that tight. It sags a bit in the middle, so I was expecting something a bit firmer. In addition, the complaints that you may have read in the other reviews about the rubber "boots" covering the ends of the legs cracking and breaking are true. They broke on my cot after about a week of usage. Very poor engineering design and that's the primary reason for my middle-range score. Lastly, it's frustrating when the Amazon price drops by $20 a couple of days after I ordered it. I contacted Amazon; they refused to give me a partial refund.
text_fidelity_b: TETON Sports Outfitter XXL Camping Cot; Camping Cots for Adults; Folding Cot Bed; Easy Set Up; Storage Bag Included

What I have discovered is that the rods be placed such that the tension is adjusted in an clockwise motion when facing the rod for the Chin-up. The Chin-up action can cause the rod to move clockwise downwards even with the clamps in place and the tendency for the rods to loosen is avoided. Unfortunately though the tension increases and can cause your door frame to creak and damage. The silicone pads at the ends will also lean outwards and the only way to prevent that is by doing the Chin-up from inside the room which is highly inconvenient.

text_fidelity_a:
MidTen Magnetic Bore Sight, Red or Green Laser Bore Sight Kit Multiple Caliber, Professional Laser Bore Sighter Rifling Scratch Proof, Suitable for Sighting Scopes Hunting Magnetic Connection Works perfectly magnetized to the end of the barrel. This is obviously for scoped weapons as it's diameter is too large for open sights. If you have a scoped pistol this will work for it as well, otherwise you'll want an actual caliber chamber-fitted bore sight IMO.

This is a no-brainer. No adjustments are available for the laser. It either does or doesn't do the job. To test it, simply place it on a flat level surface and roll it back and forth on the flat. The dot should maintain it's position. If it doesn't, return it for a replacement!

Remember, ALL bore sights are simply to get your rifle or pistol on paper at 25 yards without wasting a box or two of ammo trying to achieve the same result. Once there, fire a few rounds at the desired distance, adjusting your scope each time until it's zeroed in at the yardage you desire.

It doesn't matter that this bore sight isn't perfectly centered, as most aren't anyway contrary to popular belief. Even chamber fitted caliber-specific bore sights aren't perfect and you'll still need to fire a few rounds to be sure your actually sighted and zeroed in at the desired yardage. You can center this by hand on the end of the barrel. It doesn't need to be perfect and will be within a half inch or less of barrel center on target anyway.

At today's ammo prices, this will save you enough in ammo costs and time sighting in so that you'll be able to have more ammo for game or target shooting and put you in the field hunting faster than without one. It's "extremely rare" and I stress, "extremely rare" contrary to the claims here and there that a bore sight zeros you in to that 1/2" group at 100 yards. "Extremely rare". Be prepared to finalize your sighting in at 100 yards to zero with a few rounds after you get on paper.

Be knowledgeable and wise about what a bore sight is designed to do and you'll be happy with your purchase. As long as it gets you on paper so you can see your shot on the paper target in your scope or sighting monocular, the rest is up to you!

Only reason many reviewers leave less than a 5 star rating for this bore sight with few exceptions, is because they don't know how to use it or how to sight in a rifle or pistol in the first place. This is the ONLY bore sight you'll ever need to get your scoped firearms on paper for a good starting point. Like I said, the rest is up to you.

It works! If you don't know the exact procedure to zero your scope in, don't be afraid to ask for help.

I wasn't payed or compensated to state my opinion here. The above opinion comes from understanding what these tools are for, a little logic about what your trying to achieve with them, and a lot of experience. Get some if you don't have any and enjoy your firearm and it's accessories to the best they are capable of performing.
text_fidelity_b: MidTen Magnetic Bore Sight, Red or Green Laser Bore Sight Kit Multiple Caliber, Professional Laser Bore Sighter Rifling Scratch Proof, Suitable for Sighting Scopes Hunting Magnetic Connection

They do have a click when hit, but feel relatively soft.

Trajectory is typical of other premium golf balls. At least for me there's no difference.

Are they a ProV1 clone, I would say yes. Thus, I'll buy some more and probably order more than one dozen to get the discounted price from Vice.

I also bought Pro Plus balls and like them a little better, but that's a personal thing. I wouldn't hesitate to use these every round.

Regardless of Pro or Pro Plus, I definitely think you get the same ball for much less.

text_fidelity_a: Kalili 9 inch Lengthen Aluminum Alloy Y shaped Tent Stakes Tent Pegs for Camping Hiking 10 Pcs These 9-inch stakes are a welcome upgrade from the ubiquitous 7-inch versions, and offered at a reasonable price (at least when I bought them). These longer stakes work well in soft to moderately firm soil, but you still have to take care not to pound them too hard into rocks or solid tree roots or they'll bend. I like to use them with smaller tents on the windward side of the tent, to give a little better holding power than the shorter stakes offer, and on the sheltered side of larger tents, where you don't need such a strong hold (with longer stakes on the windward side). The supplied cord loops are a nice touch, making it easy to see and pull your stakes when it's time to go. Many suppliers don't include those cord loops, but I think it's a good investment to add them if they aren't included, so you're less likely to lose the stakes (because you can see the bright loops, and they make a good handle for pulling the stakes from the ground).

ANOOPSYCHE Bodyweight Fitness Resistance Trainer Kit with Body Workout Guide, Fitness Training Straps for Home or Professional Complete Body Workout Seems to be a good quality piece of workout equipment. Nice and versatile. The web strapping is a good thickness. Surprising how heavy it was in the box. I have a similar product from Golds Gym. This one from Anoopsyche is thicker and heavier.

Perhaps my favorite thing about this product is that the two handles are separate, which makes doing exercises (pushing, pulling, and foot in strap) much more comfortable than with one that is connected at the top.

A close second is the versatility in setting it up. It'll wrap around a bar or wedge in a closed door.

It also includes a strap that connects both sides to one mounting spot. Honestly, I'm not sure why. It's plenty long separated. Combined I think that it would be overly long unless your mounting to an extra high mounting spot. You could probably mount this thing ten foot off the ground with the additional strap without a problem. Personally, the handle sections alone are enough for me.

The buckles seem to be good quality buckles.

Deducting one star for quality control. The two handle straps are different lengths. Which is a mute point because the straps are adjustable. Just causes me to have to double check that I've adjusted both straps to equal lengths. You figure out pretty quick when both hands are in different positions because of different lengths. I ordered a second set at the same time for a friend. I opened that box to check the length of the straps. In that box both straps were the same length. I'll continue using the odd length ones and give the friend the even length ones for their convenience.
text_fidelity_b: ANOOPSYCHE Bodyweight Fitness Resistance Trainer Kit with Body Workout Guide, Fitness Training Straps for Home or Professional Complete Body Workout
